paragraphs: Rava’s attendant, as mentioned in [Avodah Zarah 57b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.57b.8)–[58a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.58a.1). A Rabbi Elyakim is also mentioned in [Midrash Tehillim 1:22](https://yitzchoklowy.com/text/midrash/midrash-tehillim/mizmor-1/).[^3]

notes.text: The servant phrase is clear, but the read-only Avodah Zarah57b and57a lookups did not locate Elyakim. The source locator remains for further investigation. An isolated כ precedes that citation.

The saved named Davidson Avodah Zarah 58a opening paragraph explicitly calls Elyakim Rava’s servant, supplying a match alongside Hyman’s 57b. This does not establish where a preceding-page episode began. The saved OYW Midrash Tehillim chapter 1 selection names Rabbi Elyakim but does not map Hyman’s section 22. The isolated כ remains visible; “as in” is a contextual possibility, not an established source reading. The two Elyakim occurrences are not newly merged.

Hyman prints 57b, where the dispute about the wine begins. At 58a Rava calls his attendant Rav Elyakim. In section 22 of the linked Lowy edition of Midrash Tehillim, Rabbi Elyakim interprets “the way of the wicked shall perish” (Psalm 1:6). The sources give two notices without establishing that they refer to one person.
